Article Title: Gold prices fall 35% from January peak putting gold loan borrowers at risk of losing pledged jewellery as 40% of gold-loan portfolios breach LTV limits; lenders send auction notices, seek extra collat
Article Text:
Gold prices have dropped 35% from their January peak and 11% so far in November, as markets factor in the possibility of higher US policy rates. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold loan notices

Additional collateral

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With gold prices crashing, gold-loan companies have begun sending legal auction notices to borrowers. The sharp decline in gold prices over the past two weeks has pushed loan-to-value (LTV) ratios beyond permissible limits.Gold prices have dropped 35% from their January peak and 11% so far in November, as markets factor in the possibility of higher US policy rates. The prospect of rising rates has reduced the appeal of gold, which does not generate any yield. According to lenders, the steep correction has triggered margin calls for a substantial number of customers for the first time in around four years.Nearly 40% of the gold-loan portfolios of these lenders have reportedly breached the thresholds, with the ratio exceeding 95% in some cases.The notices ask borrowers to either repay a portion of their outstanding dues or furnish additional collateral to bring their LTV ratios back within the prescribed limits. Failure to do so could result in the pledged gold jewellery being auctioned, according to an ET report.Banks and gold-loan financiers, including Muthoot and Manappuram, have told the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) that they have lowered the LTV ratio for new loans as a precautionary measure.The average has been reduced to 60%-65% from around 75%, providing lenders with a greater buffer against any further decline in gold prices, the people cited above said.In gold lending, a breach of the LTV limit is treated as a borrower default, even when the borrower has not missed a scheduled repayment.Executives at lending companies, who requested anonymity, said they are contacting affected borrowers and giving them the option of pledging additional gold or making an upfront payment to cover the margin shortfall before proceeding with an auction. Gold auctions are conducted 30 days after a legal notice has been served.Gold loans are generally short-term facilities, with borrowers often repaying the principal in a lump sum at the end of the tenure. Given this repayment structure, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has instructed lenders to ensure that the value of pledged gold remains adequate to cover the outstanding principal, accumulated interest and auction-related expenses throughout the loan period.Senior executives at major gold-loan companies said they are keeping a close watch on their portfolios, moderating fresh disbursements and stepping up collection efforts. They also warned that auctions could increase if borrowers fail to meet margin calls.Lenders generally maintain an effective loan-to-value (LTV) ratio of around 85% when customers pay interest every month. Where interest is settled at the end of the loan tenure, the ratio is typically kept lower, at 70%-72%.The fall in gold prices has pushed up LTV ratios as the value of the pledged jewellery has declined. Consider a lender that provides a loan of Rs 75,000 against gold worth Rs 1 lakh. The initial LTV in this case would be 75%. If the collateral loses 15% of its value, the ratio would rise to approximately 88%. A 25% fall would push it to 100%, even if the borrower’s outstanding loan amount remained unchanged.Data from credit information company CRIF show that the gold-loan portfolio had grown to around Rs 23 lakh crore as of September 30, representing approximately 12% of the country's Rs 185 lakh crore retail-loan market.The RBI's concern stems from the fact that a significant part of this expansion has been driven by existing customers borrowing larger amounts, renewing their loans and taking additional credit through top-ups. This growth has not been matched by a comparable rise in the number of borrowers or the volume of gold pledged, according to the ET report.Figures published by the Indian Bullion and Jewellers’ Association (IBJA) show that the price of 999-purity gold in India fell to Rs 1,21,038 per 10 grams on a rolling one-month basis, from the evening closing rate of Rs 1,41,710 per 10 grams on October 26.International gold prices have also declined sharply. The metal's price in US dollars per troy ounce fell 13% over one month and more than 25% over three months to $3,481, according to the latest data from investing.com.Meanwhile, the dollar index, which measures the US currency's strength against a basket of major global currencies, is hovering near its highest level in about two years. It traded close to 104 late Wednesday. A reading above 100 indicates relative strength in the dollar, which can reduce the attractiveness of assets denominated in other currencies.
Article Summary: Gold prices have dropped 35% from their January peak and 11% so far in November. The prospect of rising rates has reduced the appeal of gold, which does not generate any yield. The steep correction has triggered margin calls for a substantial number of customers for the first time in around four years.

Article Title: 'Mann ka na ho toh jyada acha hai': Piyush Goyal quotes poet Harivansh Bachchan on tariff chaos, India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Goyal says India-US trade deal nearing finalisation.

Mann ka ho acha, Mann ka na ho jyada acha

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the India-US trade deal will be finalized soon? Yes, it's definitely going to happen soon. No, I don’t think it will be finalized in the near future. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Invoking Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poetry, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal was nearing finalisation, with the roadmap and process for concluding the agreement beginning to take shape."The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something that held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape..." Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually.Quoting Bachchan's philosophy, Goyal said the trade disruptions were not what India had wanted, but the country had managed to turn the situation to its advantage."In a way you ask me, it reminds me of Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poetry. Today is his birth anniversary. And Sri Harivansh Rai Bachchan ji had said,(If things go my way, that's good; if they don't, that's even better). We didn't want all of these things in the world. It was not what we desired," the minister said."But still we converted whatever happened to an advantage to the India growth story, to a sustainable growth story that I think will hold you and all of us in the country, 1.4 billion Indians in good stead in the years to come," he said."Ultimately what matters is our ability to counter whatever situation comes our way," he added.Goyal's remarks come amid renewed trade uncertainty after the US Trade Representative (USTR) proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods under a Section 301 investigation into alleged structural excess capacity in manufacturing.Washington has indicated that the proposed tariff rate could be reduced to 17% if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the findings of the investigation.Goyal also said the India-European Union free trade agreement (FTA) was expected to be signed later this year and could come into effect by March or April 2027."The EU FTA will hopefully be executed and signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year," he added.Over the past five years, India has finalised nine FTAs covering 38 developed countries, providing preferential access to markets with a combined GDP of $70 trillion.Another eight to nine agreements currently under negotiation could expand India's market access to economies worth $85 trillion, he said.Goyal stated that India's economy had continued to grow despite global headwinds, including geopolitical conflicts, oil price volatility and tariff-related disruptions."Despite all of these uncertainties around the world, I think the one thing that remained constant was the world's trust in the India growth story. And we delivered on that trust," he said.India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter of the current financial year, with Goyal expressing confidence that the momentum would continue in the September quarter.Gross fixed capital formation grew by around 12 per cent, while bank credit expanded by nearly 19 per cent, reflecting continued investment and economic activity, he said.Exports stood at around $570 billion in the first seven months of the financial year, while October exports touched a record nearly $90 billion, putting India on track to meet its $1 trillion annual export target."I think we are well on track to achieve our USD 1 trillion target," Goyal said, crediting exporters, manufacturers, service providers and those in the agriculture and fisheries sectors for the growth.India has maintained that trade-related concerns should be resolved through ongoing bilateral negotiations with the US and said it was examining the latest notice issued by the US Trade Representative (USTR).New Delhi has rejected Washington's allegations of structural excess capacity in manufacturing and said it would work towards an early conclusion of the bilateral trade agreement (BTA)."India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a BTA. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations," the government had earlier said on Wednesday.The first Section 301 investigation is already facing a legal challenge in the US, while the latest action is also likely to be challenged in American courts.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said the India-US trade deal was nearing finalisation. Goyal's remarks come amid renewed trade uncertainty after the US Trade Representative (USTR) proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods. India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter of the current financial year.

Article Title: Vaidya Spaces delivers Serenity Tower ahead of schedule, reinforces 47-year track record
Article Text:
Vaidya West World, Vaidya Spaces’ multi acre project on Western Express Highway that has delivered Harmony and Serenity towers before time.

Technical expertise backed by industry recognition

Choosing Vaidya Spaces was the best decision our Society made after knowing their track record.

Their competence was proven during Covid-19 pandemic when without any project extension, over 300 families (new & existing) of the Society received their homes delivered on time by Vaidya Spaces.

I would say — find yourself a developer with a proven track record of completion and not necessarily the one who offers more,”

In a city where years of waiting and construction delays have become an accepted norm, Mumbai-based real estate developer Vaidya Spaces Private Limited (VSPL) has delivered yet another project ahead of schedule.The developer states that in its ambitious Vaidya West World, a multi-acre redevelopment project that would rehouse over 200 members along Vile Parle - Andheri, Western Express Highway, it has handed over Tower ‘Vaidya West World - Serenity’, the latest residential and commercial tower, 10 months before its RERA committed deadline. They also claimed that the first tower, ‘Vaidya West World - Harmony’, was completed and handed over within 18 months of the project’s 2024 launch. The remaining two, ‘Vaidya One Aeropolis’ and ‘Symphony’, are progressing towards their scheduled dates, the company said.Early completion stands out in a market where timelines are under scrutiny.As per Homebuyers body forum reportof March 2026, it is estimated that around 27.6 lakh homebuyers are stuck in delayed projects.According to MahaRERA data, 4,644 of the 8,212 Maharashtra housing projects that missed the April 20, 2026 deadline for quarterly progress updates were located in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Konkan belt.However, as per Vaidya Spaces , on-time project completion is a standard the company has maintained without exception across every single one of its real estate projects over the last 47 years.In 2025, Vaidya Spaces also featured among the top real estate developers of Mumbai. Based on market study conducted across MMR on developer delivery performance by Avance Insights, a market research agency and the Times Group, Vaidya Spaces received the recognition of ‘Iconic Trusted Developer of the Year’.As per Vaidya Spaces developer, it has since 1979, completed all of its projects as per or before their planned deadlines. Its first redevelopment project in Mumbai dates to 1980 as the firm describes itself as a trusted developer-of-choice in redevelopment projects.Vaidya Spaces’ technical depth is perhaps best illustrated by one of its most audacious projects, the construction of an engineering college in Versova, Mumbai, with basement below sea level. Vaidya developer states that due to the structural challenge of the building below the tidal waterline, its team was required to precisely engineer the construction schedules around the tides of the Arabian Sea, a feat VSPL (Vaidya Spaces Private Limited) states demonstrated a level of domain expertiseVaidya Spaces, headed by architect Jayant Vaidya and architect Sadhana Vaidya, is also one of the very few real estate developers that belong to a family of architects (Architecture firm D.R. Vaidya Spaces Pvt. Ltd. also received the ‘Distinguished Redevelopment Project Award’ in 2024 from the Chief Officer of the MBRR Board (Mumbai Building Repairs and Reconstruction Board, an MHADA body), at the Times Redevelopment Awards, for their project Aryavarta (formerly P&T Colony), a two-acre redevelopment project, for its on-time delivery of 300+ homes during the Covid-19 pandemic.For societies weighing redevelopment, a developer’s delivery track record and technical competence is now increasingly part of the decision making.saidAshok Kudtarkar, former Secretary, Aryavarta Co-operative Housing Society (formerly P&T Colony), Mumbai.

Article Title: China link, US curbs & new executive controversy: Why Nvidia halted AI server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries
Article Text:
Nvidia halts sales to SE Asia as US tightens curbs on China

Why has Nvidia stopped shipments to four Southeast Asian countries

What do the new US export rules say

Why is China not among the four countries

How did Megaspeed and Jensen Huang's controversy add to the scrutiny

Why has Jay Puri's relationship with Cenly Chen come under scrutiny?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia instructed its manufacturing partners to halt shipments of servers containing its advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, as the United States tightens export controls to prevent Chinese companies from accessing restricted computing technology through overseas data centres.The reported suspension follows new US export rules that seek to close a loophole allowing Chinese technology companies to remotely rent computing power from facilities operating in Southeast Asia.According to a Financial Times report, manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro Computer have informed customers in the four countries that Nvidia would not authorise their orders for shipment. The duration of the suspension remains unclear, with the move reportedly intended as a temporary measure while Nvidia and its partners assess compliance requirements under the new regulations.The development comes as Nvidia faces increased scrutiny over its business relationships in Asia and the alleged diversion of its advanced chips to China. Two separate cases involving senior Nvidia executives, Jensen Huang and Jay Puri, have also drawn attention to the company's network of business partners and the allocation of its AI processors.The immediate reason behind the reported suspension is Washington's effort to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced American AI chips indirectly through data centres located outside China.Direct exports of some of Nvidia's most advanced processors to China are already restricted under US export controls. However, Chinese technology companies have found alternative ways to access computing infrastructure without purchasing the chips themselves.Companies operating data centres in Southeast Asia purchase advanced Nvidia processors, install them in servers and rent out their computing capacity to customers. This arrangement allows overseas clients to access powerful AI computing infrastructure remotely, even when they are restricted from purchasing the underlying hardware directly.Chinese technology companies, including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, have relied on such arrangements to access computing resources in the region.Southeast Asia has consequently emerged as an important market for Nvidia, with data centre operators investing billions of dollars in infrastructure built around its processors.However, Washington believes such arrangements could undermine restrictions imposed on China's access to advanced semiconductor technology. The new rules are intended to prevent companies in countries considered high-risk from becoming indirect channels through which Chinese firms obtain restricted computing power.The US Commerce Department introduced an interim final rule titled 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors', which came into effect on November 19.The regulations introduce additional licensing requirements for exports of advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, countries identified by Washington as presenting a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.The rules also target overseas data centres that provide significant volumes of computing power to companies headquartered in countries classified by the US as national security concerns, including China.Under the framework, data centre operators, chip exporters and other entities involved in the supply chain must conduct due diligence on customers, including checking their ownership and control structures. The objective is to establish who ultimately accesses the computing resources and whether restricted entities could benefit from them.The regulations also provide an exemption for qualifying US-headquartered companies and their subsidiaries, subject to reporting requirements.Nvidia's reported decision to pause shipments appears to be a compliance measure as the company and its manufacturing partners assess how to operate under the new licensing framework.The Financial Times report said it was unclear how long the suspension would last. Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not immediately respond to requests for comment.China is not included in the list of destinations affected by the reported shipment suspension because the latest restrictions are specifically aimed at countries that could serve as transit points for advanced American computing technology.Washington already has separate export-control restrictions governing the direct sale of advanced AI processors to China.The latest measures seek to address a different problem: Chinese companies accessing the same technology through data centres operating in third countries.Under this arrangement, a company in China does not necessarily need to own an Nvidia processor. It can instead rent computing capacity from an overseas operator that has purchased and installed the hardware.The new rules seek to regulate both the physical movement of advanced chips and the remote use of computing infrastructure powered by them.Although Brazil is also included in the Commerce Department's licensing framework, the reported Nvidia shipment suspension has so far covered Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.The shipment suspension comes amid separate scrutiny of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, an Nvidia partner that rents computing capacity through its data centres.The company has come under investigation over allegations that advanced Nvidia chips or servers containing them may have been illegally diverted to China.The controversy also brought Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under scrutiny following reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive who was reportedly in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security (MSS).US intelligence officials have examined whether Chinese intelligence attempted to obtain information from Alice Huang during her association with the Nvidia chief. However, the available reporting has not established that she was specifically directed to collect information about Jensen Huang or that she passed information of substantial intelligence value to China. Beijing has rejected allegations of espionage.The controversy triggered questions about Huang's position at Nvidia. He subsequently resigned before the company's board reinstated him as CEO on November 23, following intervention by US President Donald Trump.Megaspeed's alleged role in the diversion of advanced chips has added to Washington's concerns about the extent to which overseas data centre operators could provide Chinese companies with access to restricted American technology.Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia executive who previously headed its global sales operations, has drawn attention over his relationship with Cenly Chen, former chief growth officer at US-based server maker Super Micro Computer. The couple dated for several years and married on March 7, 2026, according to The Wall Street Journal.Their relationship has come under scrutiny because Chen regularly dealt with Puri while Super Micro was seeking access to Nvidia's advanced chips for its customers. She also accompanied Super Micro CEO Charles Liang during visits to Nvidia's offices, while Puri was responsible for overseeing global sales and chip allocation.The developments have raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, particularly amid a US investigation into an alleged scheme to divert Nvidia-powered servers to China. On March 19, the Justice Department charged Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, a sales manager and a third-party broker with conspiring to smuggle more than $500 million worth of servers containing Nvidia chips into China.Prosecutors alleged that at least $510 million worth of equipment was diverted through a Southeast Asian company.Neither Puri nor Chen was named in the indictment. Super Micro was also not named as a defendant and has maintained that it was a victim of the alleged scheme. Chen denied that her relationship with Puri influenced her professional decisions, saying, “I never had to rely on personal relationships for professional gain.” She also denied involvement in chip procurement, while Super Micro said chip allocation was handled through a multi-department process.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has stopped shipments of servers containing its advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The move follows new US export rules that seek to close a loophole allowing Chinese technology companies to remotely rent computing power from facilities operating in Southeast Asia. China is not included in the list of destinations affected by the reported shipment suspension.

Article Title: Man sells gold received from parents and grandmother, buys house and seeks Rs 34.39 lakh exemption; taxman denies it and also adds Rs 25.69 lakh cash deposits as unexplained income; ITAT allows appeal
Article Text:
The taxpayer’s grounds of appeal stated that the sale proceeds had been invested in acquiring a residential property. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

The first addition of Rs 34,39,293 arose from the disallowance of an exemption claimed under Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961, in respect of long-term capital gains from the sale of gold ornaments and investment in a residential property.

of the Income-tax Act, 1961, in respect of long-term capital gains from the sale of gold ornaments and investment in a residential property. The second addition of Rs 25,68,850 was made under Section 68 in connection with cash deposits.

Why ITAT allowed taxpayer’s appeal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A taxpayer sold gold ornaments, invested in a residential property and claimed a tax exemption on the long-term capital gains. However, the taxpayer’s claim was rejected by the Income Tax Department.The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, has now sent the matter back for reconsideration after noting that the first appellate authority had not issued a fresh notice seeking further details from the taxpayer.The case concerns assessment year 2016-17. The taxpayer's claim for a Rs 34.39 lakh tax exemption on long-term capital gains from the sale of gold ornaments was rejected by the income tax authorities, who also treated Rs 25.69 lakh deposited in bank accounts as unexplained income.The two additions increased his taxable income by Rs 60.08 lakh.The taxpayer challenged the additions after the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre (NFAC), upheld the assessment in an order dated December 17, 2025.The taxpayer’s grounds of appeal stated that the sale proceeds had been invested in acquiring a residential property. The tax authorities disallowed the exemption after questioning the supporting evidence relating to the gold ornaments.He maintained that the ornaments had come from his family. In his grounds of appeal, he referred to 968 grams of gold ornaments received from his father and 310 grams from his mother. He also cited inheritance under a will from his grandmother.The CIT(A), however, found that documentary evidence had not been furnished to establish the genuineness of the gift transactions.The second dispute involved cash deposits totalling Rs 25,68,850. Of this amount, Rs 9,36,200 had been deposited in the taxpayer’s own bank accounts, while Rs 16,32,650 had been deposited in his wife's account. The authorities treated the amount as unexplained income under Section 68.The taxpayer challenged the addition, arguing that his disclosed income and the cash available to him had not been properly considered.He cited a cash balance of Rs 13,70,180 as of March 31, 2015, and referred to his regular income sources, including director remuneration, remuneration and interest from partnership firms, income from other sources and capital gains.He also disputed the addition relating to his wife's account, contending that the money belonged to her and should not have been treated as his income.His grounds referred to her remuneration income, past savings, amounts received from relatives and friends on the occasion of their marriage, and savings from household expenses. He argued that his wife was an independent taxpayer with separate sources of income.The CIT(A) had also observed that the cash deposits were not supported by documents establishing their source.The taxpayer challenged the appellate order, maintaining that his explanations and supporting material had not been properly considered before the additions were upheld.ITAT focused on the process followed by the CIT(A) in deciding the taxpayer’s appeal. It noted that no fresh notice had been issued seeking further details from the taxpayer before the appellate decision was made.The tribunal observed: “From the impugned order passed, it is noted that no fresh notice has been issued by Ld. CIT(A)/NFAC, calling on the details from the assessee.”It further stated: “The entire decision is based on the statement of facts furnished by the assessee along with Form 35.”In these circumstances, the tribunal considered it appropriate to have the issues examined again with reference to the evidence.Its order stated: “Under such circumstances we are of the opinion that the issue need to be remanded to the Ld.AO in the interest of justice to determine the issue in accordance with law having regard to the evidences furnished by the assessee.”The ITAT ultimately allowed the appeal for statistical purposes. It did not finally rule that the claimed family source of the gold had been established, that the Section 54F exemption must be granted, or that the cash deposits were satisfactorily explained.Instead, the matter was sent back for reconsideration in accordance with law, taking into account the evidence furnished by the taxpayer.Sarthak Prashar, Director, Global People Solutions, Grant Thornton Bharat explains that ITAT’s ruling is largely based on the fact that the taxpayer was not given an adequate opportunity to substantiate his claims.The CIT(A) upheld the disallowance of exemption of Rs 34.39 lakh under Section 54F and the addition of Rs 25.69 lakh under Section 68 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, without issuing a fresh notice seeking supporting documents.“From a taxpayer’s perspective, if the absence of documentary evidence was the basis for rejecting the claims, a reasonable opportunity should have been given to furnish such evidence,” he tells TOI.Prashar also points out that receiving gold and jewellery from parents and grandparents is quite common in India, and historical records may not always be available.“However, taxpayers should, wherever possible, maintain gift declarations, family confirmations, inheritance records, jewellery valuation reports and sale invoices. Similarly, bank statements, records of past withdrawals and cash flow statements can help explain the source of cash deposits. Timely and complete responses to tax notices are equally important,” he advises.What needs to be understood is that the relief granted by ITAT is procedural in nature and does not amount to a decision in favour of the taxpayer on merits. The outcome will ultimately depend on the evidence furnished by the taxpayer and its examination by the tax authorities.
Article Summary: A taxpayer sold gold ornaments, invested in a residential property and claimed a tax exemption on the long-term capital gains. However, the taxpayer’s claim was rejected by the Income Tax Department. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, has now sent the matter back for reconsideration after noting that the first appellate authority had not issued a fresh notice seeking further details from the taxpayer. The case concerns assessment year 2016-17.

Article Title: How India can secure its energy future without trying to eliminate oil, LPG, LNG imports
Article Text:
India’s most visible vulnerability is crude oil.

By Amit Kumar

Oil: high import exposure, balanced by refining strength

(The author, Amit Kumar, is Partner and Climate Ecosystem Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat)

India’s energy-security strategy is increasingly a portfolio of diversified imports, domestic production, strategic reserves, cleaner substitutes and a more flexible power system. The next step is to connect these initiatives into a measurable resilience framework.Energy security is sometimes confused with race to eliminate imports. For India, that would be an expensive and potentially misleading benchmark. A large, fast-growing economy is more secure when energy remains available and affordable not only in normal times but through geopolitical disruptions, commodity-price shocks, extreme weather and technology transitions. That requires multiple suppliers and routes, strategic stocks, domestic production where competitive, efficient demand and alternatives that can achieve scale.This is broadly the direction of current government policy. Oil and gas measures emphasise exploration, supplier diversification, refining, pipelines and strategic reserves. It also includes: household policy supporting LPG access; electricity generation through non-fossil fuel, transmission, storage and domestic manufacturing on solar cell, batteries, electrolyser etc.The policy architecture is substantial. The remaining challenge is execution across institutions and measuring security by outcomes—days of cover, route concentration, contract flexibility, grid reliability and affordability—not capacity announcements alone.India’s most visible vulnerability is crude oil. In FY2025-26, domestic crude production was about 28 million tonnes and import dependence reached 88.7%, according to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC). Yet the same system has a major strength: installed refining capacity of 258.1 million tonnes a year and petroleum-product output of 284.9 million tonnes in FY2025-26. India is therefore heavily dependent on imported crude, but comparatively capable in processing, product supply and exports.addresses the domestic-supply side through the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy and Open Acreage Licensing Program, which offer a uniform licensing framework and allow companies to propose exploration blocks. These reforms may moderate import dependence, but geology, project economics and long development cycles mean that domestic exploration should be treated as one hedge rather than a promise of self-sufficiency.. India now buys crude from a wider set of producers, while refiners retain flexibility to alter grades and suppliers. This reduces single-country exposure, although shipping chokepoints—especially the Strait of Hormuz—remain material. A cargo sourced farther away may improve route security but increase freight, insurance and working-capital costs.Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited operates 5.33 million tonnes of strategic storage at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur. The Government has approved a second phase of 6.5 million tonnes at Chandikhol and Padur through public-private partnership models. Commercial inventories held by refiners add another layer.LPG is a special case because energy security reaches directly into household welfare. India consumed roughly 31 million tonnes in FY2025-26; domestic production was about 13.1 million tonnes, leaving close to three-fifths of demand dependent on imports, according to PPAC. Gulf suppliers remain important, so supply disruption and freight costs can quickly affect the subsidy bill and retail affordability.The Government’s response combines import diversification, coastal and inland infrastructure, and the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), which has expanded access to clean cooking fuel. PMUY had released more than 10 crore connections by 2024, according to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.A proportionate next step would be to maintain geographically distributed LPG stocks, widen supplier and contract options, and target fiscal support toward vulnerable households rather than suppressing prices across the market.India consumed 68.5 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas in FY2025-26. Net domestic production was 34.3 bcm and LNG imports were 34.2 bcm, implying import dependence of about 50%, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). As of March 2026, India had eight operational LNG terminals with 53.5 million tonnes per annum of regasification capacity and 27,905 km of operational natural-gas pipelines.These figures show that the constraint is not simply terminal capacity. Utilisation differs sharply by location because pipeline connectivity, anchor demand, delivered prices and contractual commitments vary. Government plans to expand the national gas grid and city-gas networks can improve market depth, but new infrastructure needs credible demand and open, predictable access.LNG security requires a balanced procurement book:India should also complete technical and commercial assessments for underground or depleted-field gas storage. Gas is not automatically a ‘secure’ transition fuel if buyers remain exposed to spot prices without seasonal buffers.Renewables reduce exposure to imported fuels because sunlight and wind have no international commodity price. By 31 October 2026, India had 303.5 GW of renewable capacity, including 174.5 GW of solar, 59.5 GW of wind and 57.5 GW of large and small hydro. Total non-fossil capacity, including nuclear, was 312.2 GW, according to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).This progress sits within India’s announced goal of 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030. Supporting programs include Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission planning, renewable purchase obligations, production-linked incentives for high-efficiency solar modules, PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar and competitive procurement of hybrid and storage-backed power. These are different instruments and are at different implementation stages.Injection of such high capacity of renewables will require power storage of significant capacity and very soon. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) planning estimates that the system may require 47.24 GW (236 GWh) of battery storage and 26.69 GW of pumped storage by 2031-32. Meeting that requirement will depend on viable revenue models, timely transmission expansion, faster approvals, domestic supply chains and flexible demand. Similarly, domestic solar module assembly has scaled but upstream solar materials, battery minerals and power electronics can create new import concentrations. Energy security therefore requires diversified clean-technology supply chains and recycling, not merely more installations.Japan demonstrates that an import-dependent economy can build resilience through layered public and private oil stocks, mandatory industry obligations and tested emergency procedures. India need not copy Japan’s inventory scale; the transferable lesson is clear governance across strategic and commercial stocks.The European Union’s post-crisis gas policy uses seasonal storage targets, monitoring and burden-sharing to reduce winter risk. India’s climate, geology and gas-market structure differ, but minimum inventory rules for selected users and strategic storage pilots could be adapted after cost-benefit analysis. Denmark shows another principle: high shares of variable renewables are easier to manage with strong interconnection, flexible demand and regional balancing.India’s equivalent is deeper interstate coordination and a transmission system that treats balancing resources as national assets.In the next two to three years, priority should be to completing approved petroleum-reserve expansion, strengthening LPG and gas contingency protocols, improving utilisation of existing LNG and pipeline assets, and accelerating already-planned transmission and energy storage projects. The government should publish a compact energy-security dashboard covering import concentration, route exposure, stock cover, contract mix, grid congestion and affordability.Through 2030 and 2032, the emphasis should shift toward structural demand reduction: efficient vehicles and industry & public transport electrification, rooftop and distributed power, ethanol and biogas where sustainably supplied, and a grid capable of integrating the official non-fossil pipeline.Policy should remain technology-neutral about reliability: batteries, pumped hydro, hydro, nuclear, flexible thermal generation and demand response can each play roles with different costs and lead times.Total energy security is therefore better understood as the ability to absorb a shock without severe economic or social disruption. India’s plans already contain most of the necessary building blocks. The expert test is whether they are delivered in the right sequence, operated as one system and evaluated against resilience and affordability, not whether imports fall to zero.
Article Summary: India’s energy-security strategy is increasingly a portfolio of diversified imports, domestic production, strategic reserves, cleaner substitutes and a more flexible power system. The next step is to connect these initiatives into a measurable resilience framework. Energy security is more secure when energy remains available and affordable not only in normal times but through geopolitical disruptions.

Article Title: Close to where Xi hosted Trump days ago, Chinese bazaar openly sells banned Nvidia chips: Report
Article Text:
Near Trump-Xi meeting venue, Chinese bazaar openly sells banned Nvidia chips: Report

Poll Vote & Share your view What impact do you think AI chip exports are having on global supply chains? Increasing instability Improving efficiency No impact 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Just miles from the villa where US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping last week for APEC Summit, some of America's most tightly restricted AI chips are being openly sold in Shenzhen's bustling electronics market, according to a Washington Post report.The revelation comes amid heightened US scrutiny of Nvidia following reports that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a company customer who was allegedly a Chinese intelligence asset.The American newspaper found that vendors at the market were offering some of Nvidia's most advanced chips, including the Blackwell B300, despite US restrictions on their export to China.During a recent visit, one vendor quoted 20 million yuan, or around $3 million, for a server containing eight Blackwell B300 chips after contacting suppliers. Other traders quoted prices ranging from $3 million to $3.4 million for similar servers.The prices have risen sharply in recent weeks amid tighter US export controls. A vendor identified only by his surname, Wu, told The Washington Post that a Blackwell B300 server cost around $2 million two months ago.Nvidia does not publicly disclose prices for its high-end chips.However, an equivalent B300 server costs roughly $500,000 to $600,000 in the US, Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, told Washington Post.The availability of these chips in Shenzhen highlights the challenges Washington faces in enforcing restrictions aimed at preventing China from accessing advanced American technology and maintaining the US lead in artificial intelligence.Since Nvidia introduced its Blackwell series in 2024, the US has prohibited their shipment to China over national security concerns.These chips generally considered of advanced AI processors that the US restricts from being exported to major powers such as China.However, vendors told The Washington Post that restricted chips continue to reach the Chinese market through supply networks involving Hong Kong and other locations.“If I ever wanted to be a big [Chinese AI developer] and I needed a bunch of Blackwells, I would just go to Huaqiangbei and work out a deal,” Joshua Woodard, founder of Shenzhen-based supply chain consultancy Sparrows, told the newspaper.The market attracts start-ups, independent developers and foreign buyers. One vendor, Jason Cheng, said customers from Russia and Iran had been purchasing Nvidia chips from his stall for the past four or five years.“We don’t care which country a customer comes from, as long as they can pay,” Cheng said.Some traders said the products were kept in warehouses in Shenzhen and nearby Hong Kong and demanded advance deposits before allowing buyers to inspect them.Other Nvidia products, including RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000 chips, were openly displayed at the market. A vendor said these were usually sourced through Hong Kong and acknowledged their restricted status.In a statement to Washington Post, Chinese embassy spokesperson Liu Chang said, “China’s position on US chip exports to China is consistent. China opposes the US overstretching the concept of national security and abusing export control measures, which disrupt the stability of global industrial and supply chains.”The report also pointed to public procurement records showing that Chinese research institutes and universities continued to acquire export-restricted Nvidia chips through 2025 and 2026, including as recently as last month.Amid the scandal, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO but returned to the position just days later.
Article Summary: Some of America's most tightly restricted AI chips are being openly sold in Shenzhen's bustling electronics market, according to a Washington Post report. The revelation comes amid heightened US scrutiny of Nvidia following reports that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a company customer.

New Delhi: Ecommerce exports from India through Amazon’s Global Selling programme have reached $27 billion since its launch in 2015, the company said on Wednesday. The total rose by $7 billion from October 2025, matching the increase between the end of 2024 and October 2025, when it climbed from $13 billion to $20 billion.The number of registered exporters grew 20% over the past year to 2.4 lakh. Indian sellers have sold more than one billion Made-in-India products through Amazon’s overseas marketplaces since the programme began. The company is targeting $80 billion in cumulative exports from India by 2030, a further $53 billion from the current level.Srinidhi Kalvapudi, head of Amazon Global Selling India, said that overseas sales in towns such as Erode and Moradabad were spread across sellers. “Of course there are bigger sellers,” he said, adding that Amazon was seeing “meaningful participation” from a wider pool of exporters. He declined to disclose how many sellers in those towns made at least one overseas sale.Amazon data showed sellers in Erode crossed $121.5 million in overseas sales between January 2025 and September 2026. Moradabad crossed $83 million and Panipat $51 million over the same period.The US, UK, Germany and Canada remain among the biggest markets for Indian sellers on Amazon, Kalvapudi told TOI. He said that broadly reflected India’s offline export patterns. “MENA is another emerging market that we have seen,” he added, referring to the Middle East and North Africa.
Article Summary: Ecommerce exports from India through Amazon’s Global Selling programme have reached $27 billion since its launch in 2015. Article Title: Rupee in undervalued territory in October despite modest gains
Article Text:
Rupee in undervalued terretory

MUMBAI: The rupee’s inflation-adjusted trade-determined value (the real effective exchange rate or REER) recovered marginally in Oct, with the index rising to 93.14 from 92.14 a month earlier. The currency remained undervalued against its 40 trading partners, but the modest rebound suggests that some of the ground lost in recent months was being recovered.The undervaluation appears to explain RBI ’s comfort with the sharp strengthening of the rupee in Nov despite the backdrop of rising imports and a widening trade deficit.The month-on-month recovery followed RBI’s Oct 7 repo rate hike of 25 basis points to 5.5% and tighter currency derivatives rules introduced on Oct 10, which eased immediate pressure on the rupee. Over the 12 months to Oct 2026, the 40-currency REER fell from 97.14 to 93.14.The decline was also evident in the narrower six-currency basket, based on the revised 2022-23 base year, where the index dropped from 93.97 in Oct 2025 to 89.99 in Oct 2026. This points to a sustained weakening in the rupee’s inflation-adjusted value against its trading partners.RBI calculates the nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) using two trade-weighted baskets of foreign currencies, comprising 40 currencies and a narrower basket of six. The weights reflect India’s trade with each partner. A fall in the rupee against major trading currencies such as the dollar and euro pulls down the NEER.The REER adjusts the NEER for differences in inflation between India and its trading partners, using consumer price index data.
Article Summary: Rupee’s inflation-adjusted trade-determined value (the real effective exchange rate or REER) recovered marginally in Oct, with the index rising to 93.14 from 92.14. Article Title: September sees net FDI outflow of $4.9bn
Article Text:
FDI

NEW DELHI: India saw a $5 billion outflow of FDI on a net basis in Sept as companies repatriated equity of $5.9 billion, marginally higher than a year ago, while overseas investment by Indian entities shot up to $4.4 billion during the month, as against $1.9 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. At the same time, gross FDI into the country fell 18% to $5.9 billion during Sept.The net FDI numbers are the worst in several months, while the gross inflow numbers are the lowest since January, according to data released by RBI. September 2025 also saw net FDI outflows of around $3 billion.During the first half of the year, however, net FDI was 20% at $8.8 billion as gross inflows rose 14% to $60.1 billion. Outward FDI was up 18.2% to $22 billion during this period, while repatriation went up 12% to almost $30 billion. Officials said that some of the outflow is on account of overseas investors cashing out in some of the IPOs, while in a few cases Indian companies have bought a part of the equity held by their overseas partners. Govt is, however, confident of achieving the gross FDI target of $100 billion during the current fiscal.
Article Summary: India saw a $5 billion outflow of FDI on a net basis in Sept. Outward FDI was up 18.2% to $22 billion during this period, while repatriation went up 12% to almost $30 billion. Govt is, however, confident of achieving the gross FDI target of $100 billion.

Article Title: Know IBEF? Entity accused of creating excess capacity
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: “IBEF (India Brand Equity Foundation) is the major implementing vehicle for investment and export promotion of govt of India,” said USTR’s section 301 report, which proposed 25% additional tariffs on India, while identifying the agency as a key pillar in India’s push for creating "structural excess capacity" and putting on a par with the Rs 2 lakh crore production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme.USTR, which has extensively quoted govt-run IBEF, has catapulted it from a corner of Barakhamba Road to the prominence that is usually reserved for giant export promotion vehicles, such as Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) or Austrade.Quite rich and lavish for an initiative whose Rs 260 crore corpus is spartan even by India’s standards. Details notwithstanding, it points to an effort to hammer out an indictment and then frame an argument around it.While most are aware of PLI -- a key govt initiative to boost manufacturing in sectors such as electronics, pharma and processed food -- majority are unlikely to have heard of IBEF, an entity set up in 1996 for promoting Brand India. It has survived UPA and NDA regimes, albeit with periodic makeovers.IBEF describes itself as “a knowledge centre for global investors, international policy-makers and world media seeking updated, accurate and comprehensive information on the Indian economy, states and sectors”.It’s last uploaded annual report for 2024-25 lists out several promotion initiatives such as those related to basmati rice, millets, geographical indications. Besides, it highlights its digital media initiatives -- including setting up the commerce department’s social media cell.The agency is run by a govt-controlled board, which has secretaries from commerce and DPIIT as directors.While accusing India of undertaking policies and practices to create “structural excess capacity”, the USTR report said: “Implementing industrial plans to maintain and expand Indian manufacturing, setting overall targets for manufacturing and exports, such as Make in India , Production Linked Incentives, Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India), and IBEF, including by offering financial incentives to eligible companies based on their incremental sales.”It also alleged that India is tolerating inadequate labour protections, maintaining market barriers and imposing financial repression policies that have the effect of suppressing interest rates or of directing the allocation of equity and debt in a manner that results in outcomes different from those that would reflect market-oriented conditions.
Article Summary: USTR has extensively quoted govt-run IBEF. It has catapulted it from a corner of Barakhamba Road to the prominence that is usually reserved for giant export promotion vehicles, such as Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) or Austrade. Its Rs 260 crore corpus is spartan even by India's standards.

Article Title: “Not an onus on defending yourself..": Jason Kelce unleashes on NFL crackback block rule as Travis Kelce questions protection for players running without the ball
Article Text:
Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce unleashes on NFL crackback block rule(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce questions why players get extra protection on the field

Jason Kelce calls NFL crackback block restrictions the 'dumbest rule change'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis and Jason Kelce have a problem with the NFL 's restrictions on crackback blocks, and neither brother held back while discussing the rule on their podcast. During an episode of New Heights, the former Philadelphia Eagles center and Kansas City Chiefs tight end questioned why the league limits contact against players who are running without the football.The brothers believe players should take greater responsibility for protecting themselves on the field. Their criticism puts the NFL's player safety rules under the spotlight again, with Jason delivering a particularly blunt verdict on the restrictions.Travis Kelce believes players should remain alert when they move around the field, particularly during kickoff situations. The Chiefs tight end made his position clear on New Heights, arguing that players should prepare for contact rather than rely on restrictions that prevent certain blocks."You're running scot-free on the kickoff. You've got to have your antennas up. This is why crackbacks should be legal, because guys just have to be on their P's and Q's.Keep your head on a swivel, man. You're on the field," Travis Kelce said on the New Heights podcast.His argument focuses on awareness and the physical demands of football. However, crackback blocks are not entirely banned under NFL rules. The league restricts specific forms of contact based on the blocker's position, movement and the type of contact involved.The regulations aim to limit dangerous hits, particularly those involving contact against players in vulnerable positions.That distinction is at the heart of the brothers' disagreement with the rule. They want players to have greater freedom to make contact, even when defenders do not carry the football.Jason Kelce took the argument further on New Heights. The retired Eagles center questioned why players running without the football should receive additional protection when they are not attempting to catch a pass or carrying the ball."The idea that you're defenseless when you're running on the field is insane to me, the ball carrier isn't right there. You're not extending for a catch, you're not throwing a ball, you're just running, why is there not an onus on defending yourself?" Jason said on the New Heights podcast.Jason has spent years playing in the trenches, where blocking decisions often come down to split-second reactions. His experience as a former offensive lineman also gives him a different perspective on the restrictions, particularly when they limit what players can do to help their teammates.He did not stop at questioning the reasoning behind the rule. Jason also made his frustration clear with a blunt assessment of the NFL's decision."It's the dumbest rule change of all time, I hate it," Jason said on New Heights.The NFL continues to adjust its rules to address player safety, including concerns about head injuries and dangerous collisions. Crackback restrictions form part of those efforts, although the Kelce brothers believe the league has gone too far in limiting certain physical plays.Their criticism adds to the ongoing debate over how the NFL balances physicality with player protection. Travis and Jason may disagree with the league's approach, but their comments put the restrictions back in the conversation.
Article Summary: Travis and Jason Kelce have a problem with the NFL's restrictions on crackback blocks. The brothers believe players should take greater responsibility for protecting themselves on the field. Travis Kelce believes players should remain alert when they move around the field, particularly during kickoff situations.

The wider migration picture

The refusal rate for UK sponsored study visas reached 6.4% in the year to September 2026, the highest rolling rate since the year ending September 2015. Withdrawals before a decision rose by more than 370% in the peak autumn quarter. Indian students are among those affected. Study visas granted to Indian main applicants fell 29%.Sponsored study visa grants overall fell 23% to 335,801 in the year ending September 2026, and are 49% below the peak in the year ending June 2023, according to the Home Office. Applications from main applicants in July to September stood at 230,300, down 16% on a year earlier, The PIE News reported.The grant figures come from the Home Office's quarterly immigration statistics, published on November 26. The refusal rate and withdrawal figures come from an analysis of that data by Higher Insights and The Admit, as reported by The PIE News. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released provisional net migration estimates on the same day.As per The PIE News, the rolling refusal rate has more than doubled from 3.1% a year earlier. It has risen every quarter: 3.8% at December 2025, 4.4% at March 2026 and 4.9% at June 2026.The withdrawal increase works out to about 373%, by our calculation from these figures. Secondary reports of the same analysis put the refusal rate at 8.2% when Chinese applicants are excluded.Reacting to the data, the Russell Group said it was "watching the sudden rise in visa refusal rates closely," as quoted by The PIE News.New guidance took effect in June 2026 and tightened the Basic Compliance Assessment. Institutions must now keep their visa refusal rate below 5%, their course enrolment rate at or above 95% and their course completion rate at or above 85%, rising to 90% in June 2027.The Home Office said continued credibility checks, together with the higher onus on institutions to accept only genuine applicants, have led some universities to reduce sponsorship in certain countries.India remains the second largest source of sponsored students. The fall follows the wider decline in postgraduate demand. Visas for master's level study dropped 29% to 181,920, and master's courses now account for 58% of grants, down from 63% a year earlier. Grants to dependants fell 33% to 13,514.Extensions onto the Graduate Route, the post-study work visa, fell 31% to 162,881. Indian nationals received the most, at 66,552, ahead of Pakistani (24,768) and Nigerian (20,478) nationals.The Home Office's Migrant journey report shows that 41% of those who began on a study visa in 2020 still held valid or indefinite leave to remain at the end of 2025. For that cohort, 26% had moved into a work route.Separately, the ONS estimated net migration at 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, down from 204,000 a year earlier. Visa grants and ONS migration estimates measure different things and cover different periods. Read our analysis of the ONS figures here The 5% sponsor threshold now sits below the national refusal rate. A university that crosses it risks its licence to recruit international students. Whether refusals ease or rise in the next release will show how far institutions are narrowing recruitment.In other words, the UK is still a major destination for Indian students, but fewer applications are reaching a decision, more are being refused or withdrawn, and the route that followed the degree is narrowing too.
Article Summary: UK student visa refusal rate hits 6.4%, highest since 2015, as Indian student visa grants fall 29% and university sponsorship rules tighten. Article Title: Haryana man books front-row seat and wheelchair assistance for 15-hour Toronto-Delhi flight due to diabetes and leg pain but airline shifts him to middle seat; consumer panel orders Rs 3 lakh compensa
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





GURGAON: A passenger who was made to endure a 15-hour flight in a middle seat despite paying extra for a front-row allocation on medical grounds has been awarded Rs 3 lakh compensation by a Haryana consumer commission.The passenger had booked a Delhi-Toronto return ticket for travel in June 2025. Given his diabetes, chronic leg pain and difficulty with mobility, he had specifically opted for a front-row seat on the Toronto-Delhi sector and arranged wheelchair assistance before the journey.But the seating arrangement changed when he arrived to board his return flight. Despite holding a boarding pass showing his confirmed front-row seat, he was assigned a middle-row seat. Airline staff reportedly asked him to accept the revised allocation or get off the aircraft.With limited leave sanctioned for his trip, the passenger continued with the journey. He later complained of worsening leg pain and complications associated with diabetes after reaching India, following which he underwent hospital treatment.His attempts to obtain an explanation and relief from the airline also failed to produce a resolution.After contacting its India-based reservation office by email, he was directed to a general online customer support link.The passenger subsequently approached the consumer commission, seeking Rs 10 lakh in compensation for the alleged deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The airline disputed the allegations, maintaining that it had returned the Rs 8,799 seat-selection fee to the original payment method in June 2025. It also said an email informing the passenger about the revised seating arrangement had been sent at 3.15 pm on the day of travel. The airline attributed the change to the later wheelchair assistance request and denied any negligence.The commission found that the airline had sufficient notice of the passenger's original booking, which had been made 12 days before departure. It held that any proposed alteration should have been communicated well before the day of travel.The order also pointed out that the airline could not simply change the passenger's allocation without ensuring an appropriate alternative. If the front-row seat was considered unsuitable on safety grounds, it should have arranged another option, such as an aisle or bulkhead seat, keeping his medical and mobility requirements in mind.The commission also rejected the airline's reliance on the refund as a defence. It observed that returning the seat-selection charge after the journey did not compensate for the physical discomfort experienced during the flight or the expenses incurred for subsequent medical treatment.Holding the airline responsible for deficiency in service, the commission ordered it to pay Rs 3 lakh compensation to the passenger within 45 days.
Article Summary: The passenger had booked a Delhi-Toronto return ticket for travel in June 2025. Given his diabetes, chronic leg pain and difficulty with mobility, he had specifically opted for a front-row seat on the Toronto-Delhi sector. But the seating arrangement changed when he arrived to board his return flight.

Article Title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after $6.3 billion crypto heist
Article Text:
Binance suffered due to a mssive heist

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Where do the stolen funds stand?

NEW DELHI: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has completed work to restore its withdrawal systems following last month's $6.3 billion cyber heist, the company said on Thursday. However, withdrawals on a small number of blockchain networks remain temporarily suspended due to routine maintenance, separate from the security incident."Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted," Binance said in a post on X."Withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. Separately, a small number are temporarily paused due to network maintenance, which is standard practice," it added.The announcement marks the completion of a phased restoration process that began on November 1, after the exchange suspended withdrawals for more than two days following the attack. Customers withdrew a net $4.7 billion from the platform when services first reopened, according to Binance's November 2 update.What happened in the $6.3 billion Binance heist?The cyberattack took place on October 29, when hackers gained unauthorised access to Binance's hot wallets, which are cryptocurrency wallets connected to the internet, and stole tokens worth approximately $6.3 billion.The attackers targeted wallets across 10 different blockchains, with most of the funds transferred within a roughly 20-minute window, according to blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs.Binance's initial investigation pointed to a potentially compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer as an entry point. The company later said it had identified additional points of compromise. The FBI and blockchain intelligence firms linked the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking group.Following the breach, Binance temporarily halted withdrawals while it reviewed its security systems and worked to contain the losses. The exchange assured customers that their funds were safe and committed to absorbing the financial impact of the stolen assets.Binance has said it has the financial resources to cover the losses and will not pass the cost on to customers. Meanwhile, approximately $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue the affected tokens.However, blockchain researchers say the remaining funds are being moved through lesser-known cryptocurrency services in an elaborate money-laundering operation. Tracking and recovering the assets could take months or even years.
Article Summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has completed work to restore its withdrawal systems. However, withdrawals on a small number of networks remain temporarily suspended due to routine maintenance. The cyberattack took place on October 29, when hackers gained unauthorised access to Binance's hot wallets and stole tokens worth approximately $6.3 billion.

Article Title: Another Nvidia romance draws scrutiny: Jay Puri's ties to executive at a firm linked to China
Article Text:
Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia sales chief, and former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen's marriage draws scrutiny amid a US probe into alleged chip smuggling to China (Image credit: Clash Report's X)

How their professional roles overlapped

Super Micro's China-linked chip probe

How the relationship came under scrutiny

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia executive who led its global sales team, is facing scrutiny over his relationship with Cenly Chen, a former senior executive at US-based server maker Super Micro Computer. The couple dated for several years and married on March 7 this year, according to records. Their relationship has come under the spotlight amid a US investigation into allegations that Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips were diverted to China.Chen was Super Micro's chief growth officer and regularly dealt with Puri when the company was seeking access to Nvidia's chips for its customers, according to current and former employees of both companies, The Wall Street Journal reported.She also accompanied Super Micro CEO Charles Liang on visits to Nvidia's offices, where he pressed the chipmaker to supply products to the company's customers.During Super Micro sales meetings, Chen encouraged employees to approach her with questions related to Nvidia, positioning herself as the company's key contact on such matters, employees said.Puri, meanwhile, headed Nvidia's global sales team, which was responsible for deciding how the company's latest chips were allocated among customers.He joined Nvidia in 2005 after spending two decades at Sun Microsystems and working at other technology companies. He stepped back from his global sales role in July but remained a senior adviser.Chen denied that her relationship with Puri influenced her professional decisions. “I never had to rely on personal relationships for professional gain,” she said in an email as quoted in the WSJ report.She also said she was not involved in selecting or procuring chips for Super Micro. “I dealt with Super Micro’s customers and the customer decided the chips they bought,” Chen said, adding, “I was not involved in the selection or procurement of the chips.”Super Micro said Chen “did not manage Supermicro’s overall relationship with Nvidia or our procurement of Nvidia GPUs. Our relationship with Nvidia spans dozens of teams, functions and projects.” The company added that allocation of Nvidia chips to its customers was determined through a multi-department process.The scrutiny comes as Super Micro faces a US investigation into an alleged scheme to divert servers containing high-end Nvidia chips to China.On March 19, the US justice department unsealed charges against Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, a sales manager and a third-party broker. The indictment accused the three of conspiring to smuggle more than $500 million worth of servers containing Nvidia chips into China.Prosecutors alleged that the accused directed an unidentified company in Southeast Asia to place orders worth around $2.5 billion for Super Micro servers in 2024 and 2025, before diverting at least $510 million worth of equipment to China.Super Micro was not named as a defendant and has said it was a victim of the alleged scheme. Chen was not named in the indictment and said she had not been contacted by federal law enforcement. The company said it was cooperating with authorities and had cut ties with the individuals charged.Liaw has pleaded not guilty and resigned from Super Micro's board in March. The third-party broker has pleaded guilty under an agreement with prosecutors.Chen's relationship with Puri came under renewed attention after a shareholder lawsuit alleged that she played a role in Super Micro's acquisition of Nvidia chips. Short seller Muddy Waters also highlighted the couple's ties in a research report earlier this month.Chen spent nearly two decades at Super Micro after joining the San Jose-based company in 2008. She later became its chief growth officer, overseeing the sales team dealing with some of its biggest customers. She left the company after Nvidia's annual conference in March and was named CEO of cloud services company ChronoScale, which was spun out of Applied Digital, another Nvidia partner.Wes Cummins, CEO of Applied Digital and chairman of ChronoScale, said Chen had helped Applied Digital establish its cloud business and had advocated with Nvidia on behalf of customers. He acknowledged that her relationship with Puri created the appearance of a conflict of interest, but said he was unaware of Super Micro receiving any special treatment from Nvidia.Cummins also said the relationship had prevented ChronoScale and Applied Digital from accessing some Nvidia assistance available to customers because of the disclosed conflict of interest.Puri and Chen's relationship was known to people who worked with them. They were photographed together at the San Francisco Opera's annual masked gala in September 2024 and later attended a California Academy of Sciences gala in April with other Nvidia executives and their spouses.The developments come amid scrutiny of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's personal and professional relationships with executives at companies linked to allegations of chip diversion to China.Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International, another Nvidia customer. Some US officials suspect Alice Huang of having worked with Chinese intelligence.Both Megaspeed and Super Micro are dealing with justice department investigations into allegations of chip smuggling to China.
Article Summary: Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia sales chief, and former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen's marriage draws scrutiny. Their relationship has come under the spotlight amid a US investigation into allegations that Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips were diverted to China. Puri and Chen dated for several years and married on March 7 this year.

Article Title: Nvidia halts server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries amid chip scandal; China not on list: Report
Article Text:
Nvidia halts server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries amid US curbs.

Megaspeed under scrutiny over possible chip diversion

Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its advanced chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, amid tighter US export controls aimed at preventing Chinese firms from accessing restricted artificial intelligence processors through overseas data centres.The reported halt covers the four Southeast Asian countries, while China is not among the destinations named in the report.According to the FT, manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro, which integrate Nvidia chips into servers, have informed buyers in the four countries that Nvidia would not permit their orders to be shipped.The move follows new US restrictions that came into effect last week and require export licences for shipments of advanced chips to several Southeast Asian countries. Washington is seeking to close potential routes through which Chinese companies are believed to be accessing advanced AI computing power.It remains unclear whether the shipment halt is temporary or will continue as Nvidia and its manufacturing partners work to meet the new compliance requirements, the FT reported, citing three people familiar with the matter.Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours.The latest restrictions come amid increased scrutiny of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that rents computing capacity at its data centres.The company has come under scrutiny over possible illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China, as US authorities seek to prevent Chinese firms from accessing restricted processors through data centres operating outside the country.The US Commerce Department introduced the new export control rule days after reports involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy who had previously worked at Megaspeed. Nvidia's board subsequently reinstated Huang as CEO on November 23.The developments have brought renewed attention to the role of overseas data centres in providing Chinese companies access to advanced computing infrastructure despite US restrictions on direct chip exports to China.

Article Title: 44 Nvidia trades put Trump’s financial interests under spotlight after CEO’s return
