US president Donald Trump ’s investment portfolios traded shares of chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times between January and September, with the value of his holdings potentially rising by as much as $15 million after the company’s stock surged following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang.A review of Trump’s financial disclosures by BBC Verify found that his portfolios bought between $5.2 million and $17 million worth of Nvidia shares during the first nine months of the year, while selling between $4.4 million and $12 million worth.The filings, submitted to the US Office of Government Ethics, report transactions in broad value ranges rather than exact amounts, making it impossible to establish precisely how much Nvidia stock Trump traded or how many shares he held.Trump’s latest disclosure, submitted on November 5, indicated that he could have held as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30.Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday after the company’s board reinstated Huang as CEO, potentially increasing the value of Trump’s investment by $15 million.The rally followed Trump’s public involvement in Huang’s reinstatement. The president told CNBC he had spoken to Nvidia’s board and “made the deal” to bring the executive back.Nvidia said it had received input from senior US government officials before deciding Huang’s return posed no national security risk.Trump’s portfolios also held between $12.5 million and $58 million worth of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025, according to the disclosures.The White House has said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties, and that neither the president nor his family can direct or influence investment decisions.The frequent trading of Nvidia shares has nevertheless raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, particularly given Trump’s role in the company’s leadership decision and the administration’s oversight of advanced chip exports to China.Nvidia has become one of the world’s most valuable companies amid the boom in artificial intelligence. Its shares account for more than 6% of the S&P 500, making it one of the most influential stocks in the index.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump traded shares of chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times between January and September. The value of his holdings could rise by as much as $15 million after the company’s stock surged following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang.

Article Title: US approves Musk's SpaceX plan to deploy 1 million satellites for AI data centres in space
Article Text:
SpaceX had previously sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites. The network currently has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit. (AI image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorised Elon Musk 's SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites that will function as data centres in space, as the company seeks to meet rapidly growing demand for artificial intelligence computing.The FCC said on Wednesday it had approved SpaceX's proposed "Starmind" constellation of orbital computing modules which would process massive amounts of data and transmit it back to Earth.SpaceX had earlier sought permission to deploy up to 1 million satellites to support AI computing infrastructure in space.The FCC said the approval would allow SpaceX "to pioneer emergent technology that advances American leadership in space and artificial intelligence".Data centres are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, requiring enormous amounts of electricity to run and cool computing systems.SpaceX has proposed powering its orbital data centres using solar energy, arguing that the technology could significantly reduce energy costs and the environmental impact associated with conventional data centres on Earth."By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance costs, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers," SpaceX told the FCC.The company plans to use its next-generation Starship rocket which is currently under development to deploy the constellation.The ambitious proposal depends heavily on Starship's ability to lower launch costs and carry large numbers of satellites into orbit.FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the approval would help the US strengthen its position in artificial intelligence and expand computing infrastructure."America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence. Under President Trump's leadership, the United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people. The FCC supercharges that effort today by granting, for the first time ever, authorization to deploy 1 million orbital compute modules for data centers in space. This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth," Carr said."Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment. This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," he added.The FCC has also approved SpaceX's request to establish backup communications for its optical network. The system will use radiofrequency links for emergency telemetry, tracking and command operations, as well as backup connectivity across the satellite network.The approval allows communications in the 18.8–19.3 GHz bands for downlinks and 28.6–29.1 GHz bands for uplinks.It remains unclear whether SpaceX will eventually deploy the entire constellation. There are currently around 17,000 satellites in orbit, and deploying 1 million would represent an unprecedented expansion of satellite infrastructure, Reuters reported.Satellite operators often seek approval for larger constellations than they ultimately intend to deploy, allowing flexibility as their technology and business plans evolve.SpaceX had previously sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites. The network currently has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit.Amazon's satellite unit Leo and other competitors have questioned SpaceX's proposed constellation arguing that deploying the entire network could take centuries and that the company may not launch all the satellites it has sought approval for.Carr dismissed the criticism in March, saying, "Amazon should focus on getting Amazon's house in order with their own launches and their own satellite constellation, rather than worrying about other people that are actually out there ​launching satellites at the pace and cadence that SpaceX is."Under the approval, SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033 and launch at least 10% of the approved constellation, or 100,000 satellites by November 2035 and deploy 50% by November 2038.
Article Summary: SpaceX had earlier sought permission to deploy up to 1 million satellites to support AI computing infrastructure in space. The company plans to use its next- generation Starship rocket which is currently under development to deploy the constellation. SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033 and launch at least 10% of the approved constellation.

Article Title: US GDP growth revised sharply higher to 4.3% in third quarter on strong consumer spending, AI investment
Article Text:
US economy expands at 4.3% annualised rate in Q3, nearly double Q2 growth (representative image)

Domestic demand remains strong

Corporate profits rise at slower pace

Inflation remains a concern

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US economy grew at a faster-than-expected annualised rate of 4.3% in the July-September quarter of 2026, significantly higher than the earlier estimate of 3.4%, as stronger consumer spending and business investment supported economic activity.The revised estimate, released by the commerce department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Wednesday, marked the fastest pace of growth in three years. Economists polled by Reuters had expected the figure to be revised up to 3.5%.The economy had expanded at an annualised rate of 2.2% in the April-June quarter, meaning growth nearly doubled in the third quarter.The upward revision reflected stronger-than-previously estimated consumer spending and investment. The BEA said real GDP was revised up by 0.9 percentage point from its advance estimate, primarily due to upward revisions in these two components.Consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the US economy, rose at a revised rate of 4.2%, compared with the earlier estimate of 3.8%.Business investment also remained strong. Spending on equipment increased at an annualised rate of 21.8%, up from the previously estimated 20.9%.According to Reuters, business investment has recorded double-digit growth for three consecutive quarters, although economists have warned that this pace could slow as investors scrutinise valuations of artificial intelligence companies.The BEA said the acceleration in economic growth compared with the second quarter primarily reflected stronger investment and an upturn in government spending, partly offset by a decline in exports.Imports also increased during the quarter, according to the BEA data.A key measure of domestic demand, real final sales to private domestic purchasers, which excludes inventories, trade and government spending, rose at an annualised rate of 5.8%.This was the fastest increase since the second quarter of 2021 and higher than the earlier estimate of 4.9%.The upward revision in investment was led primarily by intellectual property products, particularly software, while stronger consumer spending reflected increased expenditure on goods, including pharmaceuticals, computer software and accessories, and petrol and other energy products.Higher-income households were driving much of the consumer spending, supported by gains in stock market wealth before the recent AI-led sell-off.Historically low layoffs and moderate hiring have also helped other households sustain expenditure, although wage growth has at times lagged inflation. Households have also been saving less and drawing on their accumulated savings.Despite the stronger economic expansion, the increase in corporate profits moderated during the quarter.Profits from current production rose by $206 billion in the July-September period, compared with an increase of $384 billion in the preceding quarter, the BEA said.The income-side measure of economic activity also showed strong growth. Gross domestic income (GDI) increased at an annualised rate of 4.4% in the third quarter, compared with a 2.3% rise in the second quarter.The average of GDP and GDI, which is considered a broader measure of economic activity, also grew at a rate of 4.4%.The revised GDP figures came alongside fresh inflation data that showed continued price pressures in the US economy.The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% year-on-year in October, matching a three-year high recorded in May.The increase was accompanied by higher energy prices and a rise in non-durable goods inflation. The PCE inflation rate remained well above the Federal Reserve's long-term target of 2%, which it has missed for almost six years.The quarterly PCE price index rose by 2.1%, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, stood at 2.5%, according to the BEA figures.The Federal Reserve had held interest rates steady at its October meeting after raising them in September. With inflation continuing to run above its target, the possibility of another rate increase at its December meeting remained in focus.The strong growth figures underline the resilience of the US economy despite headwinds, including President Donald Trump's tariff policies and higher energy prices linked to the war on Iran.The AI investment boom has also supported economic activity, while economists have pointed to a widening gap between higher- and lower-income households in their ability to sustain spending.
Article Summary: US economy expands at 4.3% annualised rate in Q3, nearly double Q2 growth.Domestic demand remains strong but corporate profits rise at slower pace. Inflation remains a concern as Federal Reserve continues to focus on interest rates.

Article Title: US proposes new tariffs on India, 13 other trade partners; China faces additional 20% duty
Article Text:
No tariffs are proposed on goods from Mexico and Norway for now (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With ANI inputs)

The Donald Trump administration on Wednesday proposed fresh tariffs on 14 of Washington's major trading partners, including India, citing concerns over "excess industrial capacity" and its adverse impact on US commerce, Reuters reported.The proposed measures follow an eight-month investigation conducted by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) under Section 301, which examined alleged unfair trade practices involving 16 trading partners.The countries and trading blocs targeted by the proposed tariffs include China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.However, Mexico and Norway have been left out of the proposed measures for now.A senior US official told Reuters that Washington had determined that these countries "create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors" through policies and practices considered "unreasonable' and "harmful" to US commerce.India and Vietnam, in particular, are among the countries that have yet to conclude trade agreements with the US.China is expected to face the highest cumulative tariff burden. The proposed 20% duties would come in addition to tariffs of around 25% imposed during Trump's first presidential term.However, the new duties would not be levied over the 10% or 12.5% tariffs introduced in July over allegations that certain countries had failed to adequately enforce anti-forced labour laws.Beijing, however, has rejected the allegations, arguing that its exports are driven by the country's competitive advantages, Reuters reported.Meanwhile, the US official also said the proposed measures would adhere to tariff limits established under existing trade agreements. These include a 15% ceiling for the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, and a 19% limit for Malaysia.Specific tariff rates for each trading partner were expected to be outlined in a notice to be published in the US Federal Register on Wednesday.Before the measures can take effect, they will be subject to a public notice-and-comment process and a hearing. According to the official, implementation could be pushed back to January 2027.The Trump administration has repeatedly accused China of flooding international markets with manufactured goods, including steel, aluminium, electric vehicles and solar products, by maintaining excess production capacity.
Article Summary: The Donald Trump administration on Wednesday proposed fresh tariffs on 14 of Washington's major trading partners, including India. The proposed measures follow an eight-month investigation conducted by the Office of the United States Trade Representative. The countries and trading blocs targeted by the proposed tariffs include China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70.The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound, however, failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.Anthropic shares tumbled 6.5% to $81.90, slipping below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, just days after the AI startup's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.The stock opened at $111.50 on November 19, with its fully diluted valuation briefly exceeding $2 trillion. However, it has since lost ground amid a broader technology selloff.Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares, making it the biggest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion listing in June.CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth over $280 million a day after the IPO, according to a filing late on Monday.The company's rapid reversal has renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and the massive investments being made in computing infrastructure, particularly as higher interest rates could increase financing costs, Reuters reported.Anthropic is not the first major technology company to fall below its IPO price soon after listing. SpaceX took about a month to slip below its offer price, while Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.Nvidia shares fell 5.9% as investors reassessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the political and governance risks surrounding the company.The chipmaker had surged nearly 30% on Monday after Huang's reinstatement, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025.Technology stocks led the declines on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 technology sector falling 2.8%. The semiconductor index dropped 7.9%, reflecting renewed selling in AI-linked companies.Before Monday's rally, AI stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned whether the sector's debt-fuelled spending on infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.Investors are also looking ahead to Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge watched by the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting.Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. Fed funds futures traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a rate hike in December and a 66% chance of another increase in January, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point towards tighter monetary policy.Investors were also wary of potential new tariffs after Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners. The findings are expected to pave the way for new import duties on a wide range of goods.The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher consumer prices in the US, adding to inflation concerns.The dollar fell 0.44% against a basket of major currencies, retreating from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes edged up 0.77 basis points to 4.928%, compared with 4.92% late on Monday.The gap between two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, a closely watched indicator of economic expectations, stood at 24.3 basis points.Gold futures fell 2.67% and silver futures dropped 5.75%, pressured by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and expectations of higher interest rates.Brent crude futures settled $2.03 higher, or 2.27%, at $91.40 a barrel after a volatile session, with fresh attacks reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.

Article Title: Trump set to hit India, China, 14 others with new tariffs after probe
Article Text:
After the set​back in the US SC over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump admins had launched two probes under Section 301.​

Section 301 probe : Govt doesn’t expect any negative impact

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union, the US Trade Representative is all set to unveil its findings in the case and propose tariffs.The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week, with Bloomberg reporting that it may come in as early as Tuesday. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe, which is likely to be followed by a set of hearings, before final tariffs are announced, in around 45 days.After the setback in the US Supreme Court over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump administration had launched two probes under Section 301.While additional tariffs of 10-12.5 per cent were imposed on imports from over 50 countries, including India, for their alleged failure to prohibit the import of goods with forced labour, which harmed American exports, the outcome of the second investigation is awaited.Going by the mood here, the government does not expect any negative impact, although it maintains that there is no structural excess capacity in India and the surplus is in anticipation of higher demand in the world’s fastest-growing major economy.In fact, during deliberations with the US government too, officials have made it clear that the government has not provided subsidy or other support to create capacity, while underlining that any country which has surplus domestic production is engaged in exports.The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. In the first probe, India had managed to get concessions with the final levy of 10 per cent imposed, against 12.5 per cent, proposed initially. The outcome of the investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework, although the final levy will be known in around 45 days. Based on the final tariff, governments will engage in negotiations for “trade deals”. India is confident of negotiating a deal where its exports enjoy “comparative advantage” over rivals from the region.While the first set of tariffs related to forced labour have been challenged in US courts, even the second one is expected to face litigation, especially because USTR findings are similar for almost all countries. In the case of structural excess capacity, among the top 20 trading partners for the US, all except Canada, the UK, Brazil and Australia are facing action, with the large European countries being part of the EU. The list also includes Norway, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, which are not among the top 20 partners for goods and services trade.
Article Summary: The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe. The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. The outcome of investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework.

Article Title: A low-Huanging fruit? Jensen burner may have netted Trump a $15 million windfall
Article Text:
Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump has never been shy about claiming credit for a good deal. His latest presidential intervention, however, may have delivered a whopping personal windfall: by some estimates as much as $15 million in gains on his Nvidia stock after he persuaded the company to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.Nvidia shares surged 31.5 per cent on Monday, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value after its board reversed Huang's departure, barely 11 days after he resigned following an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese spy agencies. An analysis of Trump's latest financial disclosures by the Financial Times estimated that his Nvidia holdings could have appreciated by between $1.3 million and $15 million in Monday's rally alone.The wide range reflects the imprecise nature of the disclosures, which report transactions in dollar bands rather than exact share counts. Depending on the assumptions about purchases and sales, Trump may have held anywhere between 32,000 and 370,000 shares as of September 30. His latest disclosure, filed on November 5, records several Nvidia purchases in September, including transactions in a range reaching $250,000.Crucially, it does not cover October or November, leaving unanswered the question of whether he bought or sold shares during the period immediately preceding Huang's reinstatement.The $15 million, therefore, is a potential paper gain, not a realised profit. Nor does it establish that Trump traded on inside information. But the coincidence is remarkable enough to invite questions about the intersection of presidential influence and personal financial interests, an issue Democrats -- some of whom are also accused of being on the make -- are ready to get their teeth into.Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday. "And I convinced them ... I made the deal." The MAGA boss was not merely cheering from the sidelines either. According to reports, veep JD Vance, himself a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist, also intervened over the weekend, acting as an emissary to Nvidia's boardThe board eventually capitulated, saying it had received assurances from senior US government officials that Huang's return did not pose a national security risk. Trump himself virtually absolved Alice Huang of being an intelligence operative despite leaks from the US intel about her ties to Chinese agencies, saying any beautiful woman who comes from China is usually dubbed a spy.The White House's defence about alleged Trump profiteering is that his portfolio is managed by independent third-party financial institutions, which make investment decisions without his involvement and replicate broad market indices such as the Schwab 1000. The administration has also described his assets as being held in a trust managed by his children, although the precise management arrangements have not always been explained consistently.Experts say all this does not eliminate the underlying conflict: a president can influence the fortunes of companies in which his family-controlled financial arrangements have significant exposure. Besides, Nvidia is hardly an isolated case, although the President's broader financial portfolio makes the Nvidia episode particularly striking. Trump's latest annual disclosure, covering 2025, showed that he received more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures, including World Liberty Financial, the family-backed crypto business liked to Pakistan, and his $TRUMP meme coin. The proceeds have helped swell his conventional stock and bond portfolio to an estimated $703 million to $2.6 billion by the end of last year, according to a Reuters analysis.The growing perception among critics is that the Trump family and its business associates are making off like bandits while the President presides over decisions that can move markets and determine corporate fortunes. The concern is not necessarily that every transaction is improper, but that the administration has blurred the boundary between public authority and private enrichment to an extent rarely seen in modern American politics.The Nvidia affair is particularly striking because it follows Trump's extraordinary intervention at Intel last year. After publicly questioning the national security credentials of Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and demanding his removal over his past China connections, Trump changed course following a White House meeting. The eventual arrangement gave the US government a 10 per cent non-voting stake in the struggling chipmaker, converting $11.1 billion in government grants and commitments into shares.Trump himself described the deal as something he had personally negotiated. The government became one of Intel's largest shareholders, while Tan retained his job. Nvidia now presents an even more unusual variation of the same phenomenon. Washington does not own a stake in the company, as it does in Intel. But its influence over Nvidia's leadership, export permissions and national security standing has become unmistakable. The company has effectively discovered that its boardroom decisions can require presidential blessing.The Wall Street Journal, among others, has described Nvidia as having become, in effect, a government-backed enterprise. Huang owes his reinstatement to Trump, and the company's ability to navigate its continuing legal and regulatory troubles may depend considerably on the administration's goodwill.Meanwhile, Congress, which is itself far from being a paragon of virtue, is up in arms. Raja Krishnamoorthi, the Illinois Democrat who chairs the House Select Committee on China, called Huang's reinstatement "outrageous," arguing that neither the government nor Nvidia's board had completed its investigation into what information Chinese intelligence might have obtained. He has demanded a full public congressional hearing, insisting that the American people deserve answers.Even Republicans are asking uncomfortable questions. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, always ready with colorful observations, said it was not his business to police Huang's marital conduct while calling it “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” But a relationship with someone potentially connected to Chinese intelligence was an entirely different matter because it jeopardizes national security, he said, adding that he wanted officials to explain whether export controls had been circumvented.He also called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to answer questions under oath about the handling of the suspected chip-diversion affair.The controversy is gradually feeding into a wider Washington debate about the extraordinary monetisation of political access, a debate complicated by the fact that lawmakers from both sides have been accused of minting money with insider info. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi has faced years of scrutiny over the spectacular investment returns associated with trades made by her husband, venture capitalist Paul Pelosi.
Article Summary: Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million. Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday.

Article Title: Trump gained up to $15 million from Nvidia rally after Huang’s return: Report
Article Text:
Trump could have gained up to $15 million from Nvidia rally after Huang’s return

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump ’s holdings in chipmaker Nvidia may have gained as much as $15 million in value, according to his latest financial disclosures, as cited by the Financial Times.The potential gain came after Nvidia shares surged more than 30 per cent on Monday following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as its chief executive.Trump’s financial filings with the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was submitted on November 5, indicate that he may have held as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30. Based on the maximum possible holding, the sharp rise in the stock price could have increased the value of his investment by up to $15 million.However, the disclosures do not establish the exact number of shares Trump owned or account for any purchases or sales made in October and November. The filings provide holdings and transactions in broad value ranges rather than precise figures.According to the calculations based on these disclosures, Trump could have held as few as 32,000 Nvidia shares, worth approximately $5.3 million, which would translate into a gain of around $1.3 million following Monday's rally. The maximum estimate assumes that he bought the largest possible number of shares within each reported range and sold the smallest, while the minimum estimate assumes the opposite.The surge in Nvidia shares followed the company's decision to reinstate Huang, who had stepped aside following revelations about alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected by US authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence.Trump said he had been closely involved in the decision to bring Huang back to the company, claiming he had played a role in securing the outcome.“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them . I made the deal.”Nvidia's board said it had received input from “senior levels” of the US government before deciding to reinstate Huang. “Based on that input, the board is confident that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the company said.Trump also publicly backed Huang's return, writing on social media: “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”In his CNBC interview, Trump said the prospect of losing Huang's expertise to China was a greater concern than the national security questions surrounding his reported personal relationships.“The bigger threat would be losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen. That would be a threat — to me that would be a far bigger threat,” he said, responding to a question about whether Huang's relationship with a woman reported to have links to Chinese intelligence posed a national security risk.Trump also said he had discussed Huang at length with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his visit to China last week. According to Trump, Xi had spoken highly of the Nvidia chief executive.“I know how good China is … and I said to a few people, you know, I know what (Chinese) President Xi is thinking because I would be thinking like, why don’t we make a deal with Jensen?”“President Xi was saying (Huang is) the most brilliant in the world at that business,” Trump said, recalling the conversation.“Nobody understands it but a guy like Jensen, they can’t copy it. It’s uncopyable,” Trump added.“You take a look at a little wafer, and you say the complexity of that China can’t copy. Nobody can copy… most chips now are obsolete, and they become obsolete very quickly.”Huang has acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, who has been suspected by US authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence. Reports have also alleged relationships with two Nvidia employees. The Wall Street Journal report did not publicly identify the additional women or provide details of the relationships disclosed to the company's board.The board's decision to reinstate Huang followed a series of discussions and meetings, after which directors said they were satisfied with his candour and ability to lead the company. Nvidia also maintained that the input it received from senior US government officials had given it confidence that his return did not pose a national security risk.Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara on Monday, where he received a warm welcome from employees. Addressing staff, he thanked them and said he would be a “better CEO the second time around”.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump’s holdings in chipmaker Nvidia may have gained as much as $15 million in value, according to his latest financial disclosures. The potential gain came after Nvidia shares surged more than 30 per cent on Monday following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as its chief executive. Trump said he had been closely involved in the decision to bring Huang back to the company.

The boards of Elon Musk 's SpaceX and Tesla have appointed five directors to special committees tasked with overseeing discussions on a potential merger between the two companies, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday citing people familiar with the matter.The appointments include two directors from SpaceX, Roelof Botha and Randy Glein and three from Tesla, Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung.Musk said during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that merging his AI, robotics, electric vehicle (EV) and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate umbrella would be "a good idea".He also confirmed that the two companies had formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential merger.The committees have hired financial advisers to prepare models that will help determine their negotiating positions in a potential all-stock merger, the FT reported.SpaceX has hired Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, while Tesla has appointed Evercore as its adviser, according to the report.The bankers are also assessing areas of overlap between the businesses and how a combined company could be structured.A potential merger would face significant regulatory challenges, particularly because of SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's dependence on China, the report said.Bloomberg reported earlier this month that a deal could be announced as early as December, citing progress in merger negotiations.

Article Title: 1.14 lakh startups generate more than 12 lakh jobs in India: Finance ministry
Article Text:
Finance Ministry

NEW DELHI: More than 1.14 lakh startups in India have created over 12 lakh jobs so far, the finance ministry said in its latest review of the Indian economy.In the report titled, ‘The Indian Economy: A Review January 2024’, the Department of Economic Affairs said that the 1.14 lakh startups recognised by the government under the 'Startup India initiative’ created more than 12 lakh jobs (as of October 2023).The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023, the document read.Despite facing global challenges in 2023 like valuation issues, few IPOs, regulatory changes and macroeconomic and geopolitical trends, India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year.The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion (from 2019 to 2023), according to a recent report by Nasscom in collaboration with Zinnov.“In 2023, despite facing global economic and regulatory challenges, Indian tech startups have prioritised the imperative of enhancing their business fundamentals, driving profitability and growth,” said Debjani Ghosh, President, Nasscom.“The proliferation of tech startups in tier 2 and 3 cities marks the ecosystem's resilience,” she added.Navigating 2024, tech startup founders expect to continue the revenue growth path with measured steps focusing on optimising expenditure and maximising profitability for B2B tech startups.Investments in deeptech will continue an upward trend in 2024. With generative AI (GenAI) acceleration, 70 per cent of start-up founders are embedding artificial intelligence (AI) in their solutions.As funding becomes scarce for the Indian startup ecosystem in general, the explosion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has given a new lease of life to entrepreneurs and founders in the country, as the Centre extends support to the sector.
Article Summary: The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023. India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year. The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion.

Article Title: Startups Revolutionizing Carbon Dioxide into Valuable Products
Article Text: For most perfume makers, ingredients to make it smell great are the most important feature. But for Stafford Sheehan, a cofounder and chemist at Air Company, the most important part of perfume-making has no scent at all.New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. While the pale yellow-color Air Eau de Parfum is about 50% more expensive than Coco Chanel’s signature No. 5, Sheehan says his product is uniquely valuable: Every 50-milliliter bottle uses 3.6 grams of CO2 that otherwise would have been released into the atmosphere. Its package reads: “Turning CO2 into something beautiful.”While the volume of CO2 utilized in the bottle is extremely small, Air Company’s perfume showcases one way the coming wave of captured carbon can be put to use. Renewable energy and electric cars alone won’t be enough to cut CO2 emissions to zero. The world will almost certainly need to capture billions of tons of the gas annually in the coming decades. Large amounts will likely be stored underground.Using it — so-called carbon capture and utilization, or CCU — to create new products from perfume to jet fuel could be an important tool in the fight against climate change, too, though the nascent industry has major hurdles to overcome.Roughly 230 million tons of CO2 are utilized every year, according to a 2019 report by the International Energy Agency. While roughly one-third of that is reused to force more oil from the ground — hardly a carbon-neutral process — CCU advocates say that the number of companies coming up with new uses for carbon has mushroomed in recent years, paving a way to unlock climate benefits. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology and lower costs.Calgary-based CleanO2 transforms CO2 captured from building heating boilers into feedstock to make soap. Newlight Technologies, a biotechnology startup based in California, takes carbon pulled directly from the air and turns it into biodegradable plastics. Germany’s Covestro AG, one of the world’s largest polymer manufacturers, is also switching some of its fossil fuel-based feedstocks to carbon-derived materials for everything ranging from car shells to medical devices and stadium roofs.Most companies working on CO2-sequestering products are still in their infancy. To grow the emerging sector, global venture capitalists in 2022 poured nearly $500 million into carbon utilization businesses, according to the IEA. That’s in stark contrast to 2015, when barely any venture money went to technologies that utilize CO2.“It’s just a whole different landscape today than it was a decade ago,” says Sasha Mackler, executive director of the energy program at Washington, DC-based non-profit Bipartisan Policy Center.Jennifer Holmgren, chief executive officer of LanzaTech Global Inc., has experienced the shifting sentiment firsthand. The Illinois-based company uses a carbon-eating bacteria – discovered in the guts of rabbits and preserved as powder – to make alternative ethanol in bioreactors not dissimilar to how breweries ferment beer. In the early 2010s, when Holmgren touted carbon-derived ethanol to prospective customers, her sales pitch was met with skepticism.But the tide began turning later that decade. In 2018, the company’s jet fuel produced from the emissions of a Chinese steel mill helped power a Transatlantic flight. LanzaTech has also inked agreements with airlines including Japan’s All Nippon Airways to supply CO2-derived jet fuel. And LanzaJet, the company’s spin-off, plans to start producing sustainable jet fuels at a commercial scale this year.Yet for all the hype around sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) using captured carbon, the industry is still an extremely small player. Almost every major airline in the world has pledged to use at least 10% sustainable jet fuels by 2030, yet SAF makes up only 0.1% of global aviation fuel supply — and much of it is made from sources other than captured CO2, such as used cooking oil.“There’s a lot more interest because consumers have become much more interested in buying things that are lower carbon,” says Holmgren. That’s enabled LanzaTech to expand the number of products that utilize CO2.American plastic container maker Plastipak, for instance, has partnered with LanzaTech to produce carbon-derived packaging materials, while polyester converted from LanzaTech’s ethanol has replaced its petroleum-based counterpart at a pilot scale in Lululemon shorts, Zara dresses, H&M yoga pants, On running shoes and Craghoppers jackets. Like SAF, though, there’s still a long way to go for CO2-derived polyester to reach meaningful levels of use.Momentum to grow beyond one-off products and low-scale production has also been supercharged by a growing array of regulations and incentives around the world. For instance, the Inflation Reduction Act that US President Joe Biden signed in 2022 raised the tax credit for carbon capture and utilization by more than 70% to $60 per metric ton in an effort to make costly projects more financially appealing.To keep the climate within habitable limits, the IEA estimates that carbon capture will have to grow to 7.6 billion tons of CO2 annually by mid-century. CCU will play a role, though just how big remains to be seen. Not every use case is created equal and some approaches, such as dissolving compressed CO2 in water to make carbonated beverages, only store the gas temporarily. To quantify the true climate benefit of carbon utilization, experts say third-party verification is badly needed.The rise of CCU technology comes as another key approach in President Biden’s net-zero roadmap is hitting a bit of a wall. Carbon capture and storage — that is, gathering CO2 as it’s released from a coal-fired power plant or other emissions source and sequestering it underground — has faced challenges because carbon is often captured in one place and stored in another. That requires pipelines to transport the gas, which many local communities have opposed. Blackrock-backed Navigator, for example, recently announced it was scrapping a planned 1,300-mile CO2 pipeline.Carbon utilization companies say that they can sidestep that issue by using carbon near or at where it’s captured.At its 12-acre factory in Brooklyn, Glenwood Mason Supply demonstrates how. The concrete manufacturer takes CO2 captured at a residential building by its partner company, CarbonQuest, and uses a technique licensed from low-carbon concrete startup CarbonCure to convert the compressed carbon into a powder not unlike dry ice. It then injects it into industrial mixers. There, the CO2 meets cement, sand and aggregate, setting off a series of chemical reactions. The final result is concrete blocks with CO2 sealed in.The technique not only stores carbon but it can also make the blocks marginally stronger. The company estimates that it has utilized about 100 tons of CO2 in total since 2020. Even if the blocks break down, the stored carbon won’t be released as CO2 because it’s been mineralized.“Cement is a big offender in carbon emissions,” says Constance Cincotta, founder of the concrete factory. She became intrigued by the technology and its ability to lower her company's climate impact after hearing about it at an industry conference in the early 2010s. But it wasn't until CarbonCure came on the scene a few years ago that the prospect of CO2-storing cement became tangible. Glenwood Mason then sourced CO2 locally from CarbonQuest, which captures carbon from buildings in New York. Those factors have enabled large-scale production.While Cincotta’s intended to help the planet, she and her team discovered that sinking CO2 into concrete blocks is good for the business, too. In 2019, New York City — where the majority of the company’s concrete blocks are sold — passed a regulation requiring all buildings to shrink their carbon footprint 40% by the end of the decade. Glenwood Mason’s phones have been ringing ever since, with calls from architects and property developers who want to leverage their lower-carbon building materials to cut emissions, says Jeff Hansen, the company’s vice president in architectural sales and marketing.The factory’s CO2-storing concrete blocks also caught the eye of Amazon.com Inc, which in 2022 persuaded a real estate developer to purchase roughly 50,000 blocks for the construction of a new warehouse in New York that Amazon has leased. Had Glenwood Mason not sealed CO2 in its blocks, it wouldn’t have won the contract, Hansen says. To figure out how to pack more carbon into its products, the company has set up a laboratory in its factory to test the reaction between CO2 and other concrete feedstocks under different temperatures and humidity levels.But figuring out the right formula is only one consideration. Utilizing CO2 often comes with an additional cost. As the demand for CO2-derived products climbs, that green premium is expected to go down. Yet “it’s very hard to be a cost parity with a 100-year-old industry that doesn’t even have to pay for its externalities,” says Holmgren of LanzaTech. Even with economies of scale, Holmgren estimates that carbon-containing fabrics will still likely cost as much as 20% higher than conventional ones.“It’s unlikely that we will ever be a cost parity,” she says.In addition to the cost barrier, CCU companies also have to convince end users that may be suspicious of unproven new technologies.Changing feedstocks “does come with risks,” says Keith Wiggins, chief executive officer of Econic Technologies, a British startup that specializes in making carbon-derived chemicals. To get risk-averse industries onboard, Wiggins says his company is laser-focused on those that are under consumer pressure to change course.That strategy seems to be working. Econic has teamed up with three manufacturers in the US, China and India to produce mattresses, outdoor garments and building insulation materials that utilize CO2. The first batch of products using the company’s technology are scheduled to enter the market in 2024.For all the promise of the carbon utilization industry, it remains to be seen if it can challenge the status quo. While Air Company started selling carbon-derived perfume in 2021, the startup has yet to build its first commercial plant, Sheehan says, citing the time-consuming process needed for collecting data and fine-tuning the technology for large-scale production.Fow now, the company’s demonstration facility in New York City — where CO2 and hydrogen gas flow through tubes into a reactor to form chemical reactions, aided by catalysts made from a confidential mixture of metals — is designed to yield at least 10,000 gallons of CO2-derived liquid annually. The limited production capacity has left many orders for its perfume — as well as jet fuels and Air Vodka, another popular product made from CO2 — unfilled.“We need to scale these facilities to the size of oil refineries today in order to have the impact on climate change that we want to have,” Sheehan says.
Article Summary: New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology.

Article Title: E-commerce firm Udaan raises $340 million ahead of planned IPO
Article Text: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain and boost vendor partnerships ahead of a stock market debut planned for 2025.The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt, the Bangalore-based company said in a statement Thursday. The round was led by M&G Plc and existing investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and DST Global participated.The round “fully funds our business plan,” Vaibhav Gupta, Udaan co-founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement. “It enables our continued journey of growth and profitability, positioning us well to be public-market ready in the next 12-18 months.”Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, runs an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business, though a very small part of India’s overall retail market, is expected to swell to $150 billion in sales in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co.The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas, Gupta told Bloomberg News last month.Udaan was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran the company until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.
Article Summary: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain. The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt. The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas.

Article Title: Minuscule AI startup raises $41 million to tap India growth
Article Text: A generative artificial intelligence startup targeting the Indian market raised $41 million in fresh funding, the largest such round by an early-stage AI contender in the country.Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages at price points that the country’s 1.4 billion people can afford. The Series A funding round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and participants included Silicon Valley billionaire Vinod Khosla’s Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, formerly Sequoia Capital India & Southeast Asia, Sarvam said Thursday.The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co-founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems as well as tools for creating apps for the meager compute infrastructure available to developers in India. The startup has a total of 18 employees and is just opening an office in the city."What we are showing is that you can build large language models with limited resources,” Raghavan said in a phone interview. "We are building at a smaller scale and demonstrating that these can be extremely cost and energy efficient so they can be accessed by everyone."Large language models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4 and Meta Platforms Inc.’s Llama, are powerful AI systems that understand by learning from vast amounts of diverse data from the internet and elsewhere to summarize, translate, and create text, audio and video for a wide range of applications. The rivalry to develop ever-more sophisticated models is heating up in Silicon Valley and such efforts have attracted billions of dollars in investments.
Article Summary: Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages. The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co- founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems.

Article Title: ZestMoney set to shut operations this month
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Buy now Pay Later (BNPL) startup ZestMoney has decided to shut operations. The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. ZestMoney did not comment. It is learnt that the firm will shut down by the end of this month.The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The deal was called off earlier this year after a due diligence process undertaken by PhonePe, while evaluating the potential acquisition failed to meet its bar. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.
Article Summary: The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.

Article Title: Startups will play important role in helping India become 3rd largest economy: CEA Nageswaran
Article Text:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Startups will play an important role in helping India become the third largest economy in the world, Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Union government V Anantha Nageswaran has said.Nageswaran said that tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country due to improvements in infrastructure and supportive policies of the government, according to a KSUM release.The CEA, during his Leadership Talk on the concluding day of the Huddle Global 2023 organised by the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years."In fact, I will say 7-in-7 is the buzz slogan, that is 7 trillion USD economy in seven years. Seven trillion USD economy size by 2030 is possible if India maintains its present growth trajectory, and in that journey startup entrepreneurs are going to play an important role," he is quoted as having said in the release.He was of the view that the active participation of startups in India in developing business models on the foundation of expanding physical and digital infrastructure will continue to generate efficiency, revenue and economic returns for the country."The last decade has seen an exceptional transformation in the startup landscape in India, which has emerged as the third largest ecosystem globally, with over 1.12 lakh startups presently recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) across 763 districts."Among them, more than 110 are unicorns with a total valuation of around USD 350 billion," he said.The CEA further said that the country ranks second in innovation quality.He said that innovation in India was not just limited to certain sectors as startups were solving problems in 56 industrial sectors, with 13 per cent of them from IT services, nine per cent from health and life sciences, seven per cent from education, five per cent from agriculture and five per cent from food and beverages.Nageswaran also said it was significant that 49 per cent of the startups were from tier-2 and 3 cities which have turned to be game-changers as the business advantages in these locations enable entrepreneurs to operate at lower costs as compared to tier-1 cities."Apart from improved infrastructure and the government's pro-active policies, the availability of a technically skilled talent pool is a huge advantage for startups to set up and flourish in tier-2 and tier-3 cities," he said.He said that historically there was a perception that small towns were difficult places to conduct business."...but with improved internet penetration, vastly better physical infrastructure, road, rail and air connectivity and supportive government policies, this is no longer true," he said.He also noted Kerala's startup journey has been an inspiring one.The CEA said that KSUM has served as the catalyst since its establishment in 2006 to promote change that propelled the state into the forefront of the global startup arena.KSUM is the Kerala government's nodal agency established in 2006 for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities in the state.Nageswaran said that with over 4,000 registered tech startups, 63 incubators and 10 lakh square feet of incubation space, KSUM has not only met its goal of promoting technology-based entrepreneurship but has also earned the distinguished position of being among the world's top business incubators.The November 16-18 fifth edition of Huddle Global, India's biggest beachside startup conclave, was organised by KSUM at Adimalathura beach, near Vizhinjam, here.Attended by around 1,500 delegates, the event displayed sophisticated products from emerging sectors such as robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, life sciences, space tech, blockchain, IoT, e-governance, fintech, healthtech, agritech, edutech and SaaS from across the country.
Article Summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country. CEA said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years.

Article Title: E-Commerce startup Udaan to trim costs ahead of 2025 IPO
Article Text: E-commerce startup Udaan is working to curb costs and forge new partnerships with consumer brands in India as it prepares to go public in 2025.Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta said in an interview. That’s set to happen around the same time as its initial public offering, he said.The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said. “Second, strategically we want to ensure that we are top of mind with shopkeepers, with big manufacturers, and we maintain our relative market share.”Lightspeed Venture Partners-backed Udaan is among startups trying to tap the rapid growth of India’s economy and consumer market, while meeting investor demands for profitability. Udaan, which at its peak employed thousands, joined fellow Indian startups in slashing jobs last year and tightening internal controls and compliance. It now has about 1,800 staff, and Gupta didn’t specify if further job cuts are needed.Corporate governance lapses at Indian online tutoring firm Byju’s, once the country’s top startup with a valuation of $22 billion, shone a light at unique challenges faced by founders in the South Asian nation and drove companies to be more diligent.“We continue to move towards more professionalized management, professionalized board and also institutionalized shareholders as we go towards public markets,” Gupta said.Udaan is yet to decide whether it will list in India or overseas. It was valued at more than $3 billion in a 2021 funding round, and was in talks to raise $400 million, Business Standard reported in September. Lightspeed owns about 35% of Udaan, while Tencent Holdings Ltd. holds 6%.The company was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran Udaan until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.Udaan built an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business still accounts for a very small part of India’s overall retail market but can balloon to $150 billion in sales and yield a 100% return on capital invested in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co. estimates published in the Mint newspaper.Bengaluru-based Udaan has also ventured into financing through its fintech unit which helps shopkeepers get working capital loans to buy inventory. That business is profitable before taxes and is growing 70% annually, Gupta said.“That’s a second business in the overall umbrella of Udaan trying to organize trade in the country,” Gupta said. “In addition to commerce, financing becomes an important market opportunity.”
Article Summary: Udaan will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta says. Udaan competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods. The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said.
